title: Small decagons of the Friday Mosque, Fatehpur Sikri
subtitle: Friday Mosque, Fatehpur Sikri, India

given.A: A point to the right of O. The lines of the big decagon touch the circle through A.

construction.note: The finished design was read from Wichmann’s SM28 drawing, whose pieces are drawn edge to edge. It is the design of his SM6 (Fatehpur Sikri decagons) with a smaller decagon and no ring of pentagons round it, so it shares that tutorial’s opening, outer ring and tile: O is the centre of a decagon, OA the inradius of SM6’s larger one, and the decagons sit at the centre and the corners of a rectangle of half-sides 2φ and 2φ tan 54°. Every other line matches the drawing within 0.001 of OA. The drawing gives no steps; we devised the construction.
construction.changes: The compass steps, their order and the named points are ours. In the drawing the small decagon’s sides are 0.6994 of OA from its centre (0.7 of SM6’s), a length no crossing of the design gives. We draw them through W, where two circles of the opening cross, at 0.6993: the pieces match the drawing within 0.0004 of OA. Colours follow the shapes, not his drawing (dark green kites, the rest white, red bands). No photograph was checked.

credits.source: Tiling Search, data206/SM28: Friday Mosque, Fatehpur Sikri, India
credits.creator: Brian Wichmann
credits.note: Read from his finished drawing, not construction instructions. His reference is E. W. Smith, The Moghul Architecture of Fathpur-Sikri, part 4 (1896), plate XXVII (Friday Mosque). He notes that Bourgoin’s plate 175 is the same pattern without some ornament, and that SM6 is the version with a ring of pentagons.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A. It crosses the horizontal line again at F.
Draw a vertical line through O. It crosses the circle at N.
Draw a circle with centre F through O. It crosses the first circle at Y1 and Y2. Draw a straight line through Y1 and Y2. It crosses the horizontal line at M, halfway from O to F.
Draw a circle with centre M through N. It crosses the horizontal line at R.

Draw a circle with centre A and opening from O to R. It crosses the circle at B and K. Draw circles of the same size round the circle, each centred where the last one crosses it. They mark C, D, E, G, H and J. The circle is now cut into ten.
Draw a line through A at 90° to the horizontal line. Turn it round O by 36°, nine times. These ten lines touch the circle at A, B, C and on round.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a line through A at 90° to the horizontal line. Draw a line through each of C, D and K at 90° to its line from O.

steps.text: Turn the vertical line round O by 36°, four times. These four lines and the vertical line run through the corners of the decagon.
The lines through A and D cross at P. The lines through C and K cross at Q. Draw a straight line through P and Q. Turn it round O by 36°, nine times. These ten lines make the outer ring.

The line through C crosses the horizontal line at P1. Draw a vertical line through P1. It crosses the line through O at 54° at K1. Draw a horizontal line through K1. Turn both new lines round O by 180°. The four lines make the tile, with corners K1, K2, K3 and K4.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: The line through C crosses the horizontal line at P1. Draw a vertical line through P1. It crosses the line through O at 54° at K1. Turn the vertical line round O by 180°. K1, K2, K3 and K4 are the corners of the tile.

steps.text: The circle with centre M crosses the circle with centre D at W. Draw a line through W parallel to the line through B. Turn it round O by 36°, nine times. These ten lines make the small decagon, with corners V1 to V10.

The right side of the tile crosses line PQ at P2, and the mirror image of line PQ at P3. Draw a line through P2 parallel to the line through E. Draw a line through P3 parallel to the line through B. Turn both new lines round O by 180°.

The right side of the tile crosses the line through W at P4, and its mirror image at P5. Draw a line through P4 parallel to the line through E. Draw a line through P5 parallel to the line through B. Draw a line through K1 parallel to the line through D. It crosses the new line through P5 at P6. Draw a vertical line through P6. Reflect the new lines in the horizontal line through O. Turn all of them round O by 180°.

The right side of the tile crosses the line through K at P7. Draw a line through P7 parallel to the line through C. The line through K1 parallel to the line through D crosses the line through V4 and V5 at P8. Draw a line through P8 parallel to the line through C. Reflect the new lines in the horizontal line through O. Turn all of them round O by 180°.
Join K1, K2, K3 and K4 to mark the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink the lines picked out in orange. They close the decagons, the pentagons and the kites.

pattern.text: Put copies of the rectangular tile side by side. A decagon sits at the centre and at each corner of every tile.
